exposure: relative contraindications to the vaginal approach
enlarged uterus (≥250 g or a size of a ≥12-week uterus)
outcome: Feasibility of OBS at the time of VH
Factors contributing to inability to perform OBS
cohort: 258 women who underwent VH and attempted OBS for benign indications between November 2014 and October 2017
finding: While opportunistic bilateral salpingectomy during vaginal hysterectomy is generally successful, lack of prolapse, obesity, and previous cesarean section were identified as risk factors for unsuccessful procedures.
mod_finding: Previous cesarean section was associated with a higher likelihood of unsuccessful opportunistic bilateral salpingectomy during vaginal hysterectomy.
